direct_claims: This chart is about global winter temperature anomalies.
It shows December, January, and February separately for the world.
The subtitle defines the measure as the difference between each month's average surface temperature and the mean temperature of the same month during 1991–2020, measured in degrees Celsius.
The source note says the data contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information and is presented by Our World in Data.
A temperature anomaly is not the absolute temperature; it is the departure from a reference average for the same month.
Because the baseline is 1991–2020, negative values mean that month was colder than the recent climatological average for that same month, and positive values mean it was warmer.
The note says the seasons are represented according to Northern Hemisphere months, and in the Southern Hemisphere these months correspond to opposite seasons.
